name: Halbai
subtitle: set rice and coconut milk pudding sweetened with jaggery and cut into soft diamonds

ingredients.note: first-press if you are extracting it fresh
dark jaggery gives the proper deep colour
scattered over the tray before setting
makes the jaggery taste like more than just sweet

prepNotes: Soak the rice at least 4 hours so it grinds completely smooth — any grit will still be there in the set pudding.
Melt the jaggery in 1 cup water, then strain it through a fine sieve to catch the grit that jaggery always carries.
Grease a shallow tray or thali with ghee and keep it beside the stove; the mixture sets fast once it comes off the heat.

steps.text: Drain the rice and grind it with 1 cup of the coconut milk to a completely smooth, pourable batter.
steps.tip: Run a little between your fingers. If it feels at all sandy, grind another 2 minutes.

steps.text: Strain the batter through a fine sieve into a heavy-bottomed pan, pushing through with the back of a ladle.
Stir in the strained jaggery syrup, the remaining coconut milk and the salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously with a flat wooden spoon, for about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Continuously means continuously. The moment you stop, the base catches and the whole batch tastes burnt.

steps.text: The mixture will thin first, then thicken and start to gloss and pull away from the sides of the pan.
Add the ghee a tablespoon at a time, letting each one be absorbed before the next goes in, about 8 minutes more.
steps.tip: When the last of the ghee starts to weep back out at the edges, it is done.

steps.text: Stir in the crushed cardamom and cook 1 minute more.
Pour into the greased tray, level the top with a ghee-smeared spatula and scatter the grated coconut over.
steps.tip: Work fast — it stiffens as it cools and will not level cleanly once it starts to set.

steps.text: Cool at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours until firm, then cut into diamonds with a greased knife.
steps.tip: Do not put it in the fridge to speed this up; chilled halbai sets hard and loses its softness.

storage: Keeps 4 days in a covered box at room temperature in cool weather, or 1 week refrigerated. Bring refrigerated pieces back to room temperature before eating, or warm them 10 seconds so the ghee softens.
